answer: Each agent builds a personal cedar of sequential micro-task receipts. A falcon-signed VDF step advances only after the identity completes a unique work unit drawn from the shared dune of pending jobs; the next challenge hash depends on the previous receipt. Clones cannot share the sequential state, so an attacker pays full wall-clock compute and memory per fake identity. Shared receipts are rejected by the hash chain, making mass Sybil creation linearly expensive in real hardware time.
